texts: good. the whenever-condition becomes a fireable rule: any sky-cat hunting on the Cliff Path triggers a gain of nightmoths at the Hollows lanterns, tied to that hunt in time, with both places and both creatures typed. One note on our side rather than your wording: "nightmoths" came out here as night_moth but as nightmoth in the next sentence, so the two sentences' moths do not yet share one symbol.

mixed: the group-level reading is right (the displaced moths keep the Hollows lanterns productive, with the productive state and its continuation recorded), but the parse also adds a rule saying each individual nightmoth keeps those lanterns, which the sentence does not claim - the effect is the swarm's jointly - and that per-moth version drops the "productive" result, so it degenerates into each moth merely holding the lanterns. Mark the joint effect so the claim stays at the group level: "Together, the displaced nightmoths keep the lanterns at the Hollows productive."
